name: Software Engineering Internship
tagline: Get ready to pass coding interviews and ship code in your first team.
description: From your first program to an internship offer. Learn Python and JavaScript properly, the computer science that interviews test, the 14 problem-solving patterns behind most coding questions, and the engineering habits teams expect: git, tests, debugging, APIs and databases. Solve real coding challenges in the browser, build portfolio projects that prove what you can do, and finish with interview and job-search playbooks.
outcome: You can solve easy and medium coding interview problems while explaining your thinking and complexity, work in a team codebase with git, tests and code review, and show a portfolio of projects with resume bullets to match.

stages.title: Programming foundations
stages.summary: Write real programs in Python and JavaScript: types, control flow, functions, data structures in the language and objects.
stages.milestone: Write a 100-line program from scratch without looking things up every line.

stages.title: Tools of the trade
stages.summary: The command line, git for yourself and for a team, regular expressions and containers.
stages.milestone: Branch, commit, open a pull request and resolve a merge conflict without panic.

stages.title: Computer science core
stages.summary: How computers represent data and run code, Big-O, the core data structures and classic algorithms.
stages.milestone: Pick the right data structure for a task and state the complexity of your code.

stages.title: Interview patterns I
stages.summary: Arrays and strings, hash maps, two pointers, sliding window, stacks and binary search: the patterns behind most easy and medium questions.
stages.milestone: Recognize the pattern in a new problem within a few minutes and solve easy problems cleanly.

stages.title: Interview patterns II
stages.summary: Linked lists, trees, heaps, graphs, backtracking, dynamic programming, greedy and bit manipulation.
stages.milestone: Solve medium tree, graph and dynamic programming problems and explain the trade-offs.

stages.title: Building real software
stages.summary: Testing, clean code, debugging, design patterns, SQL and databases, HTTP and REST APIs, and secure coding.
stages.milestone: Build and test a small API backed by a database, and review someone else's code usefully.

stages.title: Systems and scale
stages.summary: Operating systems, concurrency, and system design from the basics to an interview-ready approach.
stages.milestone: Talk through the design of a URL shortener or chat app, with numbers and trade-offs.

stages.title: Get hired
stages.summary: Behavioral interviews, your resume and portfolio, the internship search and your first 30 days.
stages.milestone: A one-page resume with project bullets, a story bank, and applications in flight.

resources.title: NeetCode roadmap
resources.note: More problems per pattern than Recurse ships, with a video walkthrough of each, for extra reps.

resources.title: LeetCode
resources.note: Online assessments use this style of problem and editor, so a few timed sessions there remove surprises.

resources.title: Tech Interview Handbook
resources.note: A second, community-maintained view of resumes and interviews to compare with Recurse playbooks.

resources.title: CS50x
resources.note: Great lectures if you want to hear the fundamentals explained a second way, especially C and memory.

resources.title: The Missing Semester
resources.note: Short MIT lectures that deepen the shell, git and editor habits teams expect.

resources.title: Pro Git
resources.note: The full reference when you hit an unusual git situation at work.

resources.title: System Design Primer
resources.note: Many more worked system design examples once the Recurse basics feel solid.

resources.title: GitHub Student Developer Pack
resources.note: Free hosting, domains and tools, so your portfolio projects can be live, not just code.
